guides.name: Unclog a toilet with a plunger
steps: Stop flushing. If the bowl is near the rim, turn off the valve behind the toilet.
Lay old towels around the base to catch splashes.
Tilt the plunger in so the cup fills with water, then seat it over the drain hole.
Push gently, then pull back hard; repeat 10 to 15 times without breaking the seal.
Lift the plunger and watch the water. If it drains, flush once to test.
Still blocked after a few rounds? Use a toilet auger instead.
safety: Never mix drain chemicals with plunging; they can splash back on you.
stopIf: Water backs up into a tub or floor drain when you flush.
Several drains in the house are slow at the same time.
A toy, phone or other solid object went down.

sources.title: How to Plunge a Toilet - Korky
sources.quote: Insert the plunger at a 45-degree angle, allowing the plunger head to fill with water.

sources.title: How To Unclog A Toilet - American Standard
sources.quote: Do not try to unclog your toilet by continuously flushing it.

guides.name: Clear a stubborn toilet clog with an auger
steps: Pull the crank so the cable is fully inside the guide tube.
Set the curved end of the tube in the drain hole, rubber guard against the bowl.
Turn the crank clockwise while pushing it down to feed the cable through the trap.
When it stops, turn back and forth and push gently to break up or hook the clog.
Crank while pulling the cable back up, then flush once to test.
Rinse and dry the cable before storing it.
safety: Keep the guard against the porcelain; a bare cable can scratch the bowl.
stopIf: The cable goes in its full length and the toilet is still blocked.
Other drains back up when you flush.
Water leaks around the base of the toilet.

sources.title: How to Use RIDGID K-6P Powered Toilet Auger | RIDGID Tools
sources.quote: Pull the Crank Handle to retract the cable into the guide tube and carefully insert the guide tube into the toilet drain.

guides.name: Fix a running toilet: replace the flapper
steps: Check the flush-valve size (2 or 3 in.) before buying the flapper.
Turn off the valve behind the toilet and flush to empty the tank.
Unhook the chain from the handle lever and lift the old flapper off its pegs.
Wipe the valve seat clean so the new flapper seals.
Hook on the new flapper and clip the chain with one or two links of slack.
Turn the water on, let it fill, and flush a few times to check.
stopIf: Water keeps running over the top of the overflow tube (fill valve problem).
The shutoff valve won't turn or it leaks.

sources.title: How to Replace Toilet Flapper - Korky
sources.quote: Be sure only to leave one to two chain links in slack.

sources.title: How to Replace a Toilet Flapper | Install Toilet Flapper | Fluidmaster
sources.quote: To remove the existing flapper, first turn off the water to the toilet and flush toilet tank emptying most of the water.

guides.name: Replace a toilet fill valve
steps: Turn off the valve behind the toilet, flush, and sponge out the last water.
Put a bucket under the tank and unscrew the supply line from the valve.
Remove the nut under the tank and lift out the old fill valve.
Set the new valve height so its top sits below the overflow tube top, then install it.
Hand-tighten the nut and supply line; add only a small turn with a wrench.
Attach the small refill hose to the overflow pipe, turn the water back on and adjust the fill level.
Check under the tank for drips over the next hour.
safety: Overtightening can crack the tank; snug is enough.
stopIf: The shutoff valve is stuck or drips when you turn it.
The tank is cracked or water seeps between tank and bowl.

sources.title: How to Replace Toilet Fill Valve - Korky
sources.quote: Too high: The valve won't shut off, and you run the risk of the valve constantly running or overflowing.

guides.name: Clear a slow shower or sink drain (hair clog)
steps: Remove the drain cover or stopper; some lift out, others unscrew.
Clean the hair and soap off the cover itself.
Push the barbed tool into the drain, twist it, then pull it out slowly.
Clean the tool off and go again until nothing more comes up.
Run hot tap water for a minute, then put the cover back.
safety: Do not use the tool after pouring in drain cleaner; it can splash back on you.
stopIf: More than one drain is slow or backing up.
You hear gurgling or smell sewage.
The clog comes back within days.

sources.title: How to Unclog a Shower Drain with a Hanger | Delta Faucet Blog
sources.quote: To unclog a shower drain with a wire hanger, remove the drain cover, straighten the hanger and bend a small hook into one end, feed it into the drain, twist gently to catch the hair, and pull it out.

guides.name: Replace a showerhead
steps: Unscrew the old head counterclockwise, holding the shower arm so it doesn't twist.
Pick off old tape and scale from the arm threads.
Wrap new thread tape clockwise around the threads 3 or 4 times.
Screw on the new head by hand; check that its rubber washer is in place.
Turn on the water. If it drips, tighten a little more with a wrench and a cloth.
stopIf: The shower arm is loose in the wall or leaks behind the tile.
The arm threads are broken or badly corroded.

sources.title: How To Install A Shower Head - American Standard
sources.quote: Step 3: Twist on the new shower head. Tighten with a wrench if necessary to prevent water from leaking.

guides.name: Clean or replace a faucet aerator
steps: Close the drain so small parts can't fall in.
Unscrew the aerator at the spout tip by hand; wrap pliers in a cloth if it is tight.
Note the order of the screen and washer as you take them apart.
Soak the parts in white vinegar for 30 minutes to loosen scale.
Brush and rinse, then reassemble in the same order and screw it back on.
Run the water. If flow is still weak, fit a new aerator of the same size.
stopIf: Flow is weak even with the aerator off (the problem is inside the faucet).
Both hot and cold are low at every faucet in the house.

sources.title: Faucet Aerator Cleaning - Moen Solutions
sources.quote: Over time, aerators can accumulate debris and mineral deposits, which can restrict water pressure or distort the spray pattern.

sources.title: Kitchen Faucet: Low Flow - Moen Solutions
sources.quote: Remove any debris and reinstall. Test the water. If the problem persists replace the spout aerator.

guides.name: Replace a kitchen faucet
steps: Close both valves under the sink (or the main), then open the faucet to drain it.
Clear the cabinet, put a bucket under the lines and take a photo of the hookup.
Disconnect the supply lines, loosen the mounting nuts from below and lift out the old faucet.
Clean the sink deck, then set the new faucet and tighten its mounting nut from below.
Connect the supply lines hand-tight, then a quarter turn more with a wrench.
Open the valves slowly and check every joint with a dry paper towel.
Remove the aerator, run water for a minute to flush debris, then refit it.
safety: Valves that haven't been turned in years can start leaking; turn them gently.
stopIf: The shutoff valves won't close fully or they leak.
Pipes under the sink are corroded or the drain must be rerouted.
You rent: ask the landlord before changing fixtures.

sources.title: DIY Kitchen Faucet Installation | Step-by-Step Guide - Moen
sources.quote: The faucet you’re replacing may also have a water shutoff valve below the kitchen sink that you can turn off instead.

sources.title: Do I need a Permit? | City of Mountain Home, Arkansas
sources.quote: Permit not needed: • Replacement of existing fixtures • leak repairs using a full circle clamp.

guides.name: Unjam a garbage disposal
steps: Switch the disposal off and unplug it or turn off its breaker.
Look in with a flashlight; remove any object with tongs or pliers, never your hand.
Fit the hex wrench in the socket under the unit and work it back and forth until it turns freely.
Wait a few minutes, then press the red reset button on the bottom.
Restore power, run cold water and switch it on.
safety: Never put your hand inside the disposal, even with the power off.
stopIf: It only hums or trips the breaker after the jam is cleared.
Water leaks from the bottom of the unit.

sources.title: How to Unjam a Garbage Disposal - Moen Solutions
sources.quote: Unplug the garbage disposal or turn off the power at the main electrical service panel.

stopIf: If you smell gas, leave the house now and call 911 or your gas company from outside.

If the tank is leaking, close the cold-water valve on top and call a plumber.

Until it is fixed, leave the gas control on its pilot or off setting.

guides.name: Replace the AC or furnace air filter
steps: Turn the thermostat to off.
Find the filter slot at the furnace or air handler, or behind a return grille.
Read the size printed on the old filter's edge (for example 16x25x1).
Slide the old one out and put the new one in with the arrow pointing toward the unit.
Close the cover and turn the system back on.
Write the date on the filter edge so you know when it is due.
stopIf: The filter compartment is wet, or there is ice on the indoor coil.
The system still blows warm air or won't start with a clean filter.

sources.title: Maintenance Checklist | ENERGY STAR
sources.quote: Inspect, clean, or change air filters once a month in your central air conditioner, furnace, and/or heat pump.

guides.name: Clean the dryer lint trap and vent
aliases: dryer takes too long to dry
steps: Clean the lint screen; wash it with soapy water if it looks clogged.
Unplug the dryer. For a gas dryer, slide it out gently without kinking the gas line.
Loosen the clamp and pull the duct off the back of the dryer.
Run the brush through the duct and the wall pipe, then vacuum up the lint.
Clear lint from the outside vent flap and check that it opens.
Reconnect the duct without crushing it, plug in and run the dryer to check airflow outside.
safety: Lint burns easily; clean the screen before or after every load.
stopIf: The vent runs to the roof or is longer than your brush reaches.
The duct is crushed, torn or made of thin foil or plastic.
You smell gas or the gas connector is damaged.

sources.title: Clothes Dryer Fire Safety - U.S. Fire Administration (PDF)
sources.quote: You are at higher risk of having a clothes dryer fire if you don’t clean your lint filter and dryer vents.

guides.name: Clean the dishwasher filter
steps: Pull out the bottom rack.
Twist the filter cylinder (usually a quarter turn) and lift it out with the mesh under it.
Rinse under warm water to wash off loose food.
Scrub the mesh gently with a soft brush and a little dish soap.
Wipe out the filter opening, then lock the filter back in place.
Slide the rack back in and run a normal cycle.
safety: Watch for glass shards in the filter area.
stopIf: Water still stands in the bottom after a cycle with a clean filter.
The dishwasher leaks onto the floor.

sources.title: How to Clean the Dishwasher Filters - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: As a general rule, clean your filter once a month, particularly with frequent use.

guides.name: Clean range hood grease filters
steps: Turn off the hood and let the cooktop cool.
Slide or unclip the metal mesh filters from under the hood.
Soak them in very hot water with dish soap and baking soda for 15 minutes.
Scrub with a soft brush, rinse and let them dry fully.
Or wash them alone in the dishwasher with non-phosphate detergent.
Clip the filters back in.
safety: Grease makes filters slippery; handle them over the sink.
stopIf: The filter is charcoal (not metal); it can't be washed and must be replaced.
The fan or light stops working.

sources.title: How often should I clean my filters? | Range Hoods | Broan-NuTone Support
sources.quote: The aluminum mesh grease filters should be washed in your dishwasher approximately every month depending on the amount of usage.

guides.name: Replace the refrigerator water filter
steps: Find the filter model in the manual or on the old filter, and buy the matching one.
Open the filter cover (inside top corner or in the base grille).
Turn or push to release the old filter; have a towel ready for drips.
Insert the new filter until it locks in.
Dispense water in bursts until 1 to 4 gallons have run, as the filter says.
Reset the filter light, then check for drips over the next day.
stopIf: Water leaks inside the fridge or under it after the change.
No water comes out at all with the new filter installed.

sources.title: When to Change the Water Filter - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: If the water flow to the water dispenser or ice maker noticeably decreases before 6 months have passed, you may need to replace the water filter cartridge more often.

sources.title: How to Flush the Water System in a Refrigerator - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: Some filters need 1, 2, or 4 gallons dispensed for a proper flush; refer to the water filter for specific guidelines.

guides.name: Clean refrigerator condenser coils
steps: Unplug the fridge or switch off its breaker.
Remove the base grille, or pull the fridge out to reach coils at the back.
Brush dust off the coils gently without bending fins or tubes.
Vacuum up the loose dust with a crevice tool.
Refit the grille, push the fridge back and plug it in.
safety: Don't pull or bend the water line behind an ice-maker fridge.
stopIf: The fridge stays warm or keeps running after cleaning.
You see oily residue or hear hissing near the coils.

sources.title: How and When to Safely Clean the Condenser Coils - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: Unplug the refrigerator or switch off the circuit breaker before cleaning.

guides.name: Clean a smelly washing machine
steps: Empty the drum.
Put one cleaner tablet in the drum itself, not the dispenser.
Run the Clean Washer cycle, or the hottest, largest cycle you have.
Wipe the door seal folds and the detergent drawer with a damp cloth.
Leave the door or lid open after loads so it dries.
safety: Don't mix bleach with other cleaners in the washer.
stopIf: Water leaks or stays in the drum after the cycle.
The smell is like burning or the drum won't spin.

sources.title: How to Clean Your Washing Machine | affresh
sources.quote: Use affresh® washing machine cleaner monthly or every 30 wash cycles for best results and a consistent clean.

sources.title: Cleaning Washers with affresh - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: Start the "Clean Washer" cycle. If your washing machine doesn't have a specific cycle for cleaning the washing machine, use the cycle with the highest water level and the hottest water temperature available.

guides.name: Recharge home AC refrigerant
stopIf: Meanwhile, replace a dirty air filter and keep the outdoor unit clear of leaves and debris.
If you see ice on the lines, turn cooling off and run the fan only until it melts.

sources.quote: Only EPA-certified technicians are allowed to purchase ozone-depleting substances (ODS) or non-ozone depleting substitutes used as refrigerants, with limited exceptions.

sources.title: Maintenance Checklist | ENERGY STAR
sources.quote: Check your central air conditioner's refrigerant level and adjust if necessary.

guides.name: Reset a tripped circuit breaker
aliases: half the house has no power
steps: Switch off or unplug what was running on the dead circuit.
At the panel, find the breaker that sits in the middle or points the other way.
Press the handle hard to the OFF side first, then flip it to ON.
Plug things back in one at a time; heaters and microwaves last.
If nothing tripped, look for a GFCI outlet nearby with a popped reset button.
safety: Stand on a dry floor with dry hands; never take the panel cover off.
Don't hold a breaker on or tape it in place.
stopIf: It trips again right away with everything unplugged.
The breaker or panel is hot, buzzing, scorched or smells burnt.
The breaker won't stay on or feels loose.

sources.title: How do I reset my circuit breaker? - PG&E Help
sources.quote: Call an electrician if the equipment is unplugged and the breaker continues to trip.

sources.title: How to Reset a GFCI Outlet After Lockout: A Step-by-Step Guide - Leviton
sources.quote: Unplug anything connected to the GFCI or any outlets downstream Press RESET again If it resets now, one of the devices was causing the fault

guides.name: Test and reset a GFCI outlet
steps: Unplug everything from the GFCI and the outlets after it.
Press RESET firmly until it clicks.
If it won't reset, check the breaker panel for a tripped breaker, then try again.
Press TEST: power should cut off. Press RESET again to restore it.
Plug devices back in one at a time; the one that trips it is faulty.
safety: Keep the outlet and your hands dry; wipe up any water first.
stopIf: It still won't reset with nothing plugged in and the breaker on.
The outlet is wet, cracked, warm or discolored.
Pressing TEST does not cut the power.

sources.title: How to Reset a GFCI Outlet After Lockout: A Step-by-Step Guide - Leviton
sources.quote: Unplug anything connected to the GFCI or any outlets downstream Press RESET again If it resets now, one of the devices was causing the fault

sources.title: Self-Test GFCI Indicators - Leviton
sources.quote: GFCI Receptacles should still be tested every month.

guides.name: Replace a light bulb
steps: Turn the light off at the switch and let a hot bulb cool for a few minutes.
Use a steady step stool, not a chair.
Unscrew the old bulb counterclockwise and check the base type and wattage on it.
Screw in an LED bulb with the same base, no brighter than the fixture's limit.
Switch it on to test, then recycle or toss the old bulb as local rules say.
safety: Never touch the metal socket with the switch on.
stopIf: New bulbs keep burning out quickly in the same fixture.
The socket is scorched, cracked or sparks.
The bulb breaks off in the socket.

sources.title: Learn About LED Lighting | ENERGY STAR
sources.quote: LED lighting products produce light up to 90% more efficiently than incandescent light bulbs.

guides.name: Replace a worn power strip
steps: Turn off and unplug the devices, then unplug the old strip from the wall.
Check the old strip and the wall outlet for heat marks or melting.
Plug the new strip straight into a wall outlet, never into another strip or extension cord.
Plug devices back in; keep heaters and other big loads off the strip.
Route the cord where it won't be pinched or covered by a rug.
safety: Space heaters, kettles and AC units go straight into the wall.
stopIf: The wall outlet is warm, loose or discolored.
The new strip trips or shuts off as soon as devices are plugged in.

sources.title: How to Use a Fire Extinguisher & Daisy Chaining Risks - NYC DCAS (PDF)
sources.quote: Use a longer extension cord instead of connecting multiple cords or power strips.

guides.name: Replace a worn electrical outlet
steps: Turn off the breaker for the outlet, then confirm both sockets are dead with the voltage tester.
Remove the cover plate and unscrew the outlet from the box.
Pull it out, test the wires again, then photo the hookup.
Move the wires one at a time: black to brass, white to silver, bare to green.
Wrap each wire clockwise under its screw and tighten firmly.
Fold the wires back, mount the outlet and plate, then turn the breaker on and test.
safety: Switch off the breaker and check with the tester before you touch any wire.
Use copper wire only; aluminum wiring needs special devices and an electrician.
stopIf: The wires are aluminum, scorched, brittle or too short.
The box holds more than one cable or the outlet was a GFCI.
Your city requires a licensed electrician or a permit, or you rent.

sources.title: Installing and Testing a GFCI Receptacle - Leviton instruction sheet (PDF)
sources.quote: To prevent severe shock or electrocution always turn the power OFF at the service panel before working with wiring.

sources.quote: Permit not needed: • Changing out devices Examples: switches, receptacles, lights, ceiling fans.

sources.title: Homeowners Electrical Permit Guidelines | Carlisle, MA
sources.quote: Effective immediately a homeowner may apply for and receive a permit to do electrical work in their own home with the following documentation

guides.name: Replace a light switch
steps: Turn off the breaker and confirm with the voltage tester that the switch is dead.
Remove the plate and the two mounting screws; pull the switch out.
Test the wires again, then take a photo of where each one goes.
Move the wires to the same spots on the new switch, ground to the green screw.
Tighten each screw, fold the wires in and mount the switch with ON at the top.
Turn the breaker on and test the light.
safety: Switch off the breaker and check with the tester before you touch any wire.
stopIf: It is a 3-way switch (two switches control one light) or a smart switch needing a neutral.
The wires are aluminum, scorched or brittle.
Your city requires a licensed electrician or a permit, or you rent.

sources.title: Single Pole/3-Way Toggle Switch L1461/L1463 - Leviton instruction sheet (PDF)
sources.quote: TURN OFF POWER AT CIRCUIT BREAKER OR FUSE AND TEST THAT THE POWER IS OFF BEFORE WIRING!

sources.title: Do I need a Permit? | City of Mountain Home, Arkansas
sources.quote: Permit not needed: • Changing out devices Examples: switches, receptacles, lights, ceiling fans.

guides.name: Replace a ceiling light fixture
steps: Turn off the breaker (not just the wall switch) and test the wires at the fixture.
With a helper holding it, remove the old fixture and photo the wiring.
Check the ceiling box is firmly fixed; fit the new mounting bracket to it.
Join black to black and white to white with wire connectors; ground to the green screw.
Tug each joint, tuck the wires in and fasten the fixture to the bracket.
Fit the bulbs and cover, turn the breaker on and test.
safety: Switch off the breaker and check with the tester before you touch any wire.
Work from a steady ladder and have someone hold heavy fixtures.
stopIf: There is no ground wire or the box is loose or missing.
The new fixture is heavy (over 50 lb) or a ceiling fan.
Your city requires a licensed electrician or a permit, or you rent.

sources.title: Project Source Flushmount Ceiling Light CLLR12WW - installation guide (PDF)
sources.quote: All fixtures must be mounted to an outlet box that is supported by the building structure.

sources.quote: Permit not needed: • Changing out devices Examples: switches, receptacles, lights, ceiling fans.

stopIf: If the panel is hot, smoking or smells burnt, stay away from it and call 911.
Do not remove the panel cover yourself.

sources.quote: If you are at all uncertain whether a panel is energized, do not remove its cover. Call a licensed electrician. Many jurisdictions forbid panel work by nonlicensed electricians.

guides.name: Patch a small hole in drywall
steps: Trim loose paper and crumbs from the hole edge.
For holes wider than about 1/2 inch, stick a mesh patch over the hole first.
Press spackling in with the putty knife and scrape it flat in a thin layer.
Let it dry, add a second thin coat a little wider, feathering the edges.
When dry, sand it smooth and wipe off the dust.
Prime and paint to match the wall.
safety: Wear a dust mask while sanding.
stopIf: The hole is bigger than a fist or the edges are soft or wet.
You see wires or pipes behind the hole.

sources.title: Spackling 101 | DAP
sources.quote: Apply spackling in thin layers and feather the edges

guides.name: Replace torn window screen mesh
steps: Lay the frame flat, pry out the old spline and remove the torn mesh.
Match the new spline size to the groove (bring a piece of the old one).
Tape the frame down and lay new mesh over it with extra on every side.
Roll the spline into the groove over the mesh, keeping the mesh square and snug.
Push the spline into the corners with a screwdriver tip.
Trim extra mesh along the outer edge of the groove with the knife.
safety: Cut away from your hand and change dull blades.
stopIf: The frame is bent, cracked or the corners are loose.
The screen is on an upper floor you can't remove from inside.

sources.title: How to Replace or Repair a Window or Door Screen | Phifer
sources.quote: Lay screen fabric over frame, align squarely and overlap 1/2” (1.3 cm) on all sides.

guides.name: Recaulk a bathtub or shower
steps: Cut along both edges of the old caulk and peel or scrape all of it out.
Clean the joint with rubbing alcohol and let it dry completely.
Put painter's tape on both sides of the joint for a straight line.
Cut the tip at an angle and run one steady bead along the joint.
Smooth it with the tool, then pull the tape off right away.
Keep water off it for 24 hours so it cures.
safety: Use plastic scrapers on acrylic or fiberglass tubs to avoid scratches.
stopIf: The wall behind the old caulk is soft, moldy or wet.
Tiles are loose or the tub moves when you step in.

sources.title: How to recaulk your bathtub for a fresh, mold-free finish - GE Sealants
sources.quote: Moisture under fresh sealant ruins adhesion and invites mold later.

guides.name: Replace a doorknob
steps: Measure the backset (door edge to hole center, 2-3/8 or 2-3/4 in.) before buying.
Remove the screws on the inside knob and pull both knobs apart.
Unscrew the latch plate on the door edge and slide the old latch out.
Fit the new latch flush in the edge, slanted side toward the frame, and screw it in.
Join the two knobs through the latch and tighten the screws evenly.
Test the latch with the door open, then closed.
stopIf: The door edge is split or the holes are a different size.
It is a fire-rated door or you rent and need the landlord's OK.

sources.title: Kwikset knob installation guide (PDF)
sources.quote: Hold the latch in front of the door hole, with the latch face flush against the door edge.

guides.name: Replace a deadbolt lock
steps: Measure the backset (2-3/8 or 2-3/4 in.) and the door thickness before buying.
Remove the two screws on the inside turn piece and pull both halves off.
Unscrew and remove the old bolt from the door edge.
Install the new bolt with the bolt extended and the word UP facing up.
Fit the outside cylinder through the bolt, then the inside turn piece, and tighten.
Install the strike plate with long screws and test the bolt with the door closed.
stopIf: There is no existing deadbolt hole (new holes need a boring kit).
The door is metal or fire-rated, or you rent.

sources.title: How to install a 816 deadbolt? | Kwikset
sources.quote: Measure backset (A), 2-3/8" (60mm) or 2-3/4" (70mm).

sources.title: Support for Traditional Locks | Kwikset
sources.quote: Remove the two screws located on the interior side of the door.

guides.name: Assemble flat-pack furniture and anchor it
steps: Unpack on a rug or the box, and sort and count the parts against the list.
Follow the steps in order; hand-tighten until the frame is square.
Tap dowels and panels with a rubber mallet, never a metal hammer.
Tighten all screws once the piece is standing straight.
Attach the tip-over restraint to a wall stud or the right anchor for your wall.
Put heavy items in the lowest drawers.
safety: Anchor dressers, bookcases and TVs; tip-overs can kill small children.
stopIf: Parts are missing or cracked; contact the seller instead of improvising.
You can't find a stud or a safe anchor for your wall.

sources.title: Creating Safer Homes Together - IKEA
sources.quote: Use the tip-over restraint provided with the product and the right hardware for your wall type.

sources.title: AnchorIt.gov | CPSC.gov
sources.quote: Existing furniture can be anchored with inexpensive anti-tip brackets. New furniture, such as dressers, are sold with anti-tip devices. Install them right away.

guides.name: Hang a wall shelf
steps: Find the studs with the stud finder and mark them lightly.
Hold the brackets in place, level them, and mark the screw holes.
Drill pilot holes; screw into studs wherever you can.
Where there is no stud, set a drywall anchor rated for the load.
Screw the brackets on, set the shelf and check it is level.
safety: Check for wires and pipes before drilling, especially above and below outlets and switches.
stopIf: The shelf will hold heavy things (books, TV, mirror) and you can't reach studs.
The wall is plaster, brick or tile you don't know how to anchor into.
The stud finder shows live wires where you need to drill.

sources.title: FAQs - TOGGLER
sources.quote: Moving objects away from the wall (e.g., the far end of a shelf or using a TV mount that swings away from the wall) significantly increases the effective weight of that object, greatly reducing the allowable load of that anchor.

sources.title: Creating Safer Homes Together - IKEA
sources.quote: Depending on your wall type, use the right hardware to anchor your furniture to the wall.

guides.name: Free up phone storage and restart
steps: Open Settings > General > iPhone Storage to see what uses space and the suggestions.
Apply the suggestions you agree with, such as offloading apps you never use.
Back up photos and videos, then delete large ones and apps you no longer need.
Restart: press a volume button together with the side button, then slide to power off.
After about half a minute, turn it back on with a long press on the side button.
safety: Back up anything you might want before deleting it.
stopIf: The phone restarts by itself, gets hot, or will not turn on.
It stays slow even with plenty of free space (battery or hardware).

sources.title: Restart your iPhone - Apple Support

guides.name: Put on a glass screen protector
steps: Work in a clean room with fans off so dust does not settle.
Take off the case and any old protector, then clean the screen with the kit's wet and dry wipes.
Lift any remaining dust with the dust-removal sticker.
Peel the backing, line the glass up with the edges or the tray, and lower it gently.
Press the center, then push any air bubbles out to the edges with a cloth.
stopIf: The phone's own screen is already cracked; a protector will not fix it.

sources.title: How to replace the screen protector on your phone - iFixit Repair Guide
sources.quote: Press the center of the protector so the adhesive spreads to the edges.

guides.name: Add or upgrade laptop memory (RAM)
steps: Check the manual: does it have a RAM slot, which type (e.g. DDR4 SO-DIMM) and what maximum?
Shut down, unplug the charger and disconnect the battery if you can.
Remove the bottom cover screws and ease the cover off with a plastic tool.
Touch bare metal to discharge static, and hold the stick by its edges only.
Line up the notch, insert the stick at about 45 degrees, then press down until the clips lock.
Close the cover, power on and check the new memory size in system settings.
safety: Never open the laptop while it is plugged in.
stopIf: The RAM is soldered to the board or the cover is glued shut.
It will not start after the upgrade and reseating the stick does not help.

sources.title: Lenovo ThinkPad X250 RAM Replacement - iFixit Repair Guide
sources.quote: Align the notch on your new RAM stick with the one inside the slot, and insert it at a 45-degree angle.

sources.title: How to Install an M.2 NVMe PCIe SSD | Crucial EU
sources.quote: Touch an unpainted metal surface to ground yourself.

sources.title: Crucial Laptop Memory | crucial.com
sources.quote: Yes, most BIOS will automatically detect and install new RAM.

guides.name: Swap a laptop SSD for a bigger one
steps: Check the slot type and length in the manual (for example M.2 2280 NVMe).
Back up your files to an external drive or cloud storage.
Clone the old drive to the new one through a USB enclosure, or plan a fresh system install.
Shut down, unplug, remove the bottom cover and touch bare metal to ground yourself.
Unscrew the old drive, slide it out, insert the new one at a slight angle and screw it down.
Close up, boot, and check your files and the new capacity.
safety: Do not touch the drive's gold connector pins.
stopIf: The storage is soldered to the board.
The drive is encrypted and you do not have the recovery key.
The new drive is not detected after you install it.

sources.title: How to Install an M.2 NVMe PCIe SSD | Crucial EU

sources.title: How to Install an M.2 NVMe PCIe SSD | Crucial EU

guides.name: Replace an iPhone 13 battery with a kit
steps: Back up the phone, run the battery below 25% and power it off.
Remove the two bottom screws, warm the edges and lift the screen with a suction cup and picks.
Open the screen like a book without straining its cables, and disconnect the battery first.
Pull the adhesive strips out slowly to free the old battery; never pry against the battery.
Fit the new battery and adhesive, reconnect everything and close the phone.
Charge it to 100% and take the old battery to an electronics recycler.
safety: Never puncture or bend the battery; a damaged lithium battery can catch fire.
stopIf: The battery is swollen or is already pushing the screen up.
You smell smoke or the battery gets hot: move it outdoors, away from anything that burns.

sources.title: iPhone 13 Battery Replacement - iFixit Repair Guide
sources.quote: A charged lithium-ion battery can catch fire and/or explode if accidentally punctured.

guides.name: Clean a laptop keyboard
steps: Shut down and unplug the laptop.
Tilt it back so the keyboard is steep but not standing straight up (about 75°).
Keep the can upright and the straw tip about 1/2 in. from the keys; sweep across the rows.
Tip the laptop onto one side and sweep again, then repeat on the other side.
Wipe the keys with a soft, lint-free cloth.
safety: Never spray liquid straight onto the keyboard.
stopIf: Liquid was spilled into the laptop.
Keys still do not work after cleaning.

sources.title: How to clean the keyboard of your MacBook or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
sources.quote: Hold your Mac notebook at a 75-degree angle, so it's not quite vertical.

guides.name: Swollen phone or laptop battery
stopIf: Stop using and charging the device, and power it off.
Keep it on a non-flammable surface away from heat; do not press, puncture or remove the battery.
If it smokes or gets hot, move away from it and call 911.

sources.title: Frequent Questions on Lithium-Ion Batteries | US EPA
sources.quote: Sometimes, the battery inside a product will become swollen. The swelling indicates damage to the battery and is a potential fire hazard.

guides.name: Remove mildew from shower caulk
steps: Turn on the fan or open a window, and put on gloves.
Rinse the caulk with warm water to loosen soap scum.
Spray the mildew remover on the stained caulk and keep it wet for about 10 minutes.
Scrub lightly with the brush, then rinse well with water.
Dry the area and leave the fan on for an hour.
safety: Never mix bleach cleaners with ammonia, vinegar or other cleaners.
Keep the room aired out; leave if your eyes or throat sting.
stopIf: Black spots stay after two cleanings; the mold is under the caulk, so recaulk instead.
Mold covers more than about 10 square feet.

sources.title: How to Remove Mold Stains in the Shower & Bathroom Walls | Clorox
sources.quote: Wipe the surface with the bleach solution, ensuring you cover all mold-affected areas. Keep surfaces wet for 10 minutes.

sources.title: Dangers of Mixing Bleach with Cleaners | Washington State Department of Health
sources.quote: Don't mix bleach with ammonia, acids, or other cleaners.

guides.name: Get rid of a smelly sink or garbage disposal
steps: Turn off the disposal and unplug it or switch off its breaker.
Pull out the rubber splash guard if it lifts out.
Rub a paste of baking soda and a little warm water over the guard's underside, then rinse it.
Refit the guard, restore power and run the disposal with cold water.
For a drain you rarely use, run water for a minute to refill its trap.
safety: Never reach into the disposal; use tongs for anything inside.
stopIf: The sink drains slowly or water backs up.
A sewage smell comes from several drains at once.

sources.title: How do I Eliminate Odors in a Garbage Disposal - Moen Solutions
sources.quote: Scrub the underside of the splash guard with baking soda and warm water.

sources.title: Bottle Trap Drain | Other Products | Kohler Assist
sources.quote: An inner tube acts as a barrier or "trap," preventing sewer gas from entering the atmosphere.

guides.name: Clean window screens
steps: Take each screen out and mark which window it came from.
Lay it flat on a towel and brush off loose dust.
Mix a little dish soap in warm water and scrub gently with a soft brush or cloth.
Rinse with a gentle spray or a bucket of clean water, not a pressure washer.
Shake off the water, wipe the frame and let it dry fully before refitting.
safety: Take screens out from inside the room; don't lean out of upper-floor windows.
stopIf: The mesh is torn or the frame is bent.

sources.title: How To Clean Your Window Screens | Simonton
sources.quote: Using a soft bristle brush, gently scrub your window screens with soapy water.

guides.name: Get rid of cockroaches with gel bait
steps: Clean up crumbs and grease, store food sealed and fix dripping taps.
Find where they hide: under the sink, behind the fridge and stove, inside cabinet hinges.
Put pea-sized dots of gel in cracks and corners near those spots, not on food surfaces.
Don't spray insecticide or cleaner on the bait; it keeps roaches away from it.
Check after a week and add fresh dots where the bait is gone.
safety: Keep bait out of reach of children and pets.
Follow the label exactly; using a pesticide against its label is illegal.
stopIf: You still see many roaches after 2 to 3 weeks.
You see roaches in daylight or in many rooms.
You live in an apartment where the building needs treatment.

sources.title: Cockroaches / Home and Landscape / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
sources.quote: When using insecticides, baits provide better control than sprays.

guides.name: Clean dirty tile grout
steps: Open a window or run the fan and put on gloves.
Sweep or rinse off loose dirt first.
Spray the grout cleaner on a small section and let it sit as the label says.
Scrub along the grout lines with the brush.
Rinse with clean water and wipe dry, then move to the next section.
safety: Use one cleaner at a time and never mix it with bleach products.
Rinse well before switching to a different cleaner.
stopIf: Grout is cracked, crumbling or missing.
Tiles are loose or sound hollow when tapped.

sources.title: How to Clean Tile Grout | Lysol US
sources.quote: it’s always best to start with less harsh cleaning products and work your way up if and when needed.

sources.title: Dangers of Mixing Bleach with Cleaners | Washington State Department of Health
sources.quote: Don't mix bleach with ammonia, acids, or other cleaners.

guides.name: Clean a small patch of mold
steps: Size it up first: these steps are only for a patch under about 10 sq ft.
Fix the leak or moisture source first, or the mold will return.
Put on an N95 mask, goggles and gloves; open a window.
Wash the moldy spots on hard surfaces with soapy water and a stiff brush.
Dry the area completely; run a fan or dehumidifier.
Bag moldy porous items like ceiling tiles or carpet and throw them away.
safety: Never mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners.
Keep children and anyone with asthma out of the room.
stopIf: The mold covers more than about 10 square feet or follows a large leak or flood.
Mold is inside walls, in air ducts, or keeps coming back.
Someone in the home has asthma, allergies or a weak immune system.

sources.quote: If the moldy area is less than about 10 square feet (less than roughly a 3 ft. by 3 ft. patch), in most cases, you can handle the job yourself

sources.title: Dangers of Mixing Bleach with Cleaners | Washington State Department of Health
sources.quote: Don't mix bleach with ammonia, acids, or other cleaners.

guides.name: Replace wiper blades
steps: Look up both blade lengths for your car; driver and passenger sizes often differ.
Lay a towel on the windshield, then lift one wiper arm away from the glass.
Press the small tab where the blade meets the arm and slide the old blade off the hook.
Slide the new blade onto the hook until it clicks, then tug gently to check it is locked.
Lower the arm slowly onto the towel, then do the other side.
Remove the towel and test the wipers with washer fluid.
safety: A bare wiper arm can snap back and crack the glass; keep a hand on it.
stopIf: The wiper arm is bent or the wipers do not move at all (motor or linkage problem).

sources.title: Car and Truck Wiper Blades Replacement - iFixit Repair Guide
sources.quote: Cover the windshield with a towel or blanket to avoid shattering the windshield if the wiper arms come down accidentally after the blades are removed.

guides.name: Replace the cabin air filter
steps: Find the filter in the owner's manual; it is often behind the glove box on the passenger side.
Empty the glove box, unhook its damper arm and press in the sides so it swings down.
Unclip the filter cover and note the airflow arrow on the old filter before you pull it out.
Slide in the new filter with its arrow pointing the same way.
Refit the cover and glove box, then run the fan on high to check the airflow.
stopIf: The filter is under the hood behind other parts, or the dash has to come apart.
The vents still smell musty with a new filter (the system may need cleaning).

sources.title: How to Change Cabin Air Filter | FRAM
sources.quote: The cabin air filter is usually located on the passenger side of the vehicle under the dash behind the glove compartment or under the hood.

guides.name: Replace the engine air filter
steps: With the engine off, open the hood and find the air box at the end of the big intake hose.
Release the clips or screws on the lid and lift it without forcing it.
Note how the old filter sits, lift it out and wipe loose dirt from the box.
Set the new filter in the same way so its rubber edge seals all around.
Close the lid, refasten every clip and check nothing is pinched.
safety: Do not run the engine with the air box open.
stopIf: The air box is buried under other parts or needs a sensor unplugged that you are unsure about.
You find oil inside the air box.

sources.title: How to Change Your Car's Engine Air Filter | FRAM
sources.quote: Note how it sits in the housing and do the same with the new filter to ensure good airflow and filtration.

guides.name: Check and fill car tire pressure
steps: Find the recommended cold pressure on the sticker in the driver's door jamb, not on the tire.
Measure cold: after the car has sat for about 3 hours or driven only a short way.
Unscrew a valve cap, press the gauge straight onto the valve and read it.
If it is low, add air in short bursts and measure again each time.
If it is high, press the valve pin briefly to let air out, then measure again.
Do all four tires and the spare, then put the caps back on.
safety: Never go above the maximum pressure printed on the tire sidewall.
stopIf: A tire keeps losing air, or has a nail, cut or bulge.
The pressure light stays on after every tire is at the right pressure.

sources.title: Tire Safety Ratings and Awareness | TireWise | NHTSA
sources.quote: To get an accurate tire pressure reading, you must measure tire pressure when the tires are cold or compensate for the extra pressure in warm tires.

guides.name: Top up windshield washer fluid
steps: With the engine off and cool, open the hood and find the cap with the windshield-spray symbol.
Pour the fluid in slowly and stop below the neck so it does not overflow.
Close the cap firmly and wipe up any spills.
Start the car and test the sprayers.
safety: Never pour engine coolant (antifreeze) into the washer tank; it can damage paint.
stopIf: The tank empties fast or drips under the car (a leak).
The pump hums but nothing sprays.

sources.title: Window Washer Fluid (Honda owner's manual)
sources.quote: Do not use engine antifreeze or a vinegar/water solution in the windshield washer reservoir.

sources.title: Checking the Washer Fluid Level | 2025 Hyundai Tucson
sources.quote: However, use washer solvent with antifreeze characteristics in cold climates to prevent freezing.

guides.name: Replace a halogen headlight bulb
steps: Check the manual for the bulb size (for example H11) and how to reach it.
Turn the lights off and let the old bulb cool for a few minutes.
From under the hood, unplug the connector, twist the bulb a quarter turn and pull it out.
With gloves on, hold the new bulb by its base; never touch the glass.
Twist it in, reconnect the plug and test low and high beams.
safety: This guide is for halogen bulbs; HID (xenon) and LED headlights are different.
stopIf: You would have to remove the bumper or the whole headlight to reach the bulb.
The new bulb does not light either (fuse or wiring problem).
Your car has sealed LED headlights with no bulb to replace.

sources.title: How to Change a Car Headlight Bulb (PEAK, Old World Industries)
sources.quote: The natural oils in your fingertips can cause hot spots on the bulb glass if you touch them with your bare hand, which will make them burn out super fast.

guides.name: Jump-start a dead car battery
steps: Park the good car close but not touching, turn both off and put on safety glasses.
Clip one red clamp to the dead battery's +, then the other red to the good battery's +.
Clip one black clamp to the good battery's − terminal.
Clip the last black clamp to bare, unpainted metal on the dead car's engine, away from the battery.
Start the good car, let it run 3 to 5 minutes, then start the dead car.
Remove the clamps in reverse order without letting them touch.
Drive 20 to 30 minutes so the battery can recharge.
safety: Batteries can give off explosive hydrogen gas; keep sparks and flames away.
Never let the red and black clamps touch each other.
stopIf: The battery is cracked, bulging, leaking or smells of rotten eggs: do not jump it.
The car still will not start after two tries, or it dies again soon after.
Your manual says the car needs a special jump procedure (common on hybrids and EVs).

sources.title: How to Jump a Battery and Get Yourself Back on the Road | AAA Automotive
sources.quote: The last connection is to attach the final black clamp to a clean, unpainted piece of metal on the car with the dead battery, like a thick bolt on the engine block.

guides.name: Replace a car battery
aliases: replace the battery in my car
steps: Match the new battery's group size and terminal layout to the old one.
Turn everything off, put on glasses and gloves, and mark which cable is + and which is −.
Remove the negative (black) cable first, then the positive (red).
Take off the hold-down clamp and lift the battery out with both hands; it is heavy.
Clean any corrosion off the tray and cable clamps with a wire brush.
Fit the new battery and clamp, connect positive first and negative last, then tighten.
Start the car and reset the clock or radio if needed.
Take the old battery back to the store or a recycler; never put it in the trash.
safety: Never let a metal tool touch both terminals at once.
Battery acid burns; wear glasses and gloves and keep sparks away.
stopIf: The battery is under a seat or the trunk floor, or the manual says it must be registered with a scan tool.
The cables or clamps are badly corroded or broken.

sources.title: Power Up: Tips for Replacing Your Car Battery
sources.quote: Always disconnect the negative (black) terminal cable first. Then, disconnect the positive (red) cable. This prevents accidental shorting.

guides.name: Change your own engine oil
steps: Check the manual for the oil grade, amount and filter, and buy the matching ones.
Run the engine a minute, drive onto ramps on level ground and set the parking brake.
Put the pan under the drain plug, remove the plug and let the oil drain out.
Refit the plug with a new crush washer if it uses one; snug it, do not overtighten.
Unscrew the old filter, check its rubber ring came off, oil the new ring and hand-tighten.
Pour in the new oil with a funnel, run the engine briefly and look for leaks.
Wait a few minutes, check the dipstick and top up to the full mark.
Take the used oil and filter to a recycling drop-off; never pour it out.
safety: Never get under a car held up only by a jack; use ramps or jack stands.
Engine oil can be hot; wear gloves.
stopIf: You cannot lift the car safely, or the drain plug threads feel stripped.
The old oil looks milky or has metal flakes in it.

sources.title: How to Perform Your Own Oil Change | AAA Club Alliance
sources.quote: You should NEVER get under a vehicle only supported by a jack.

sources.title: How to Change Your Own Oil: A Beginner’s Guide | Valvoline
sources.quote: If your vehicle uses a crush washer, replace it with a new one.

sources.title: Managing, Reusing, and Recycling Used Oil | US EPA
sources.quote: If you are one of the many people who change their own motor oil, you too need to know how to properly manage the used oil.

guides.name: Replace brake pads or rotors
safety: Do not blow brake dust with compressed air or a dry brush; it may contain asbestos.
stopIf: If the pedal feels soft or sinks, do not drive; have the car towed.

sources.title: EPA: Current Best Practices for Preventing Asbestos Exposure Among Brake and Clutch Repair Workers (EPA-747-F-04-004)
sources.quote: If you are not able to determine whether your brakes or clutch contain asbestos, you may want to consider having your brakes or clutch serviced at a commercial automotive shop.

sources.title: 11 Ways To Know You May Need New Brakes | AAA Automotive
sources.quote: If you apply the brakes and hear a high pitch or grinding noise, this is a strong indicator that the brakes have worn thin.

guides.name: Touch up a paint chip
steps: Find the paint code on the door-jamb sticker and buy a pen in that exact code.
Wash the spot, wipe it with rubbing alcohol on a clean cloth and let it dry.
Use the pen's abrasive tip to clear loose paint or rust from the chip only.
Shake the pen and dab thin coats of color into the chip, letting each coat dry.
Finish with the clear coat end and let it cure before washing the car.
safety: Use the paint in a ventilated place, away from flames.
stopIf: The chip is bigger than a pencil eraser, or the metal under it is rusting through.
The paint is a tri-coat pearl or matte finish.

sources.title: Scratch Fix All-in-1 Touch Up Paint | Duplicolor
sources.quote: Use the abrasive prep tip, applying pressure to the affected area to remove loose paint and rust.

guides.name: Restore cloudy headlights
steps: Wash and dry the headlights.
Mask the paint around each lens with painter's tape.
Follow the kit to remove the yellowed layer, working evenly over the whole lens.
Polish until the lens is clear, then wipe it clean.
Apply the kit's UV-protective coat and keep it dry while it cures.
safety: If your kit uses a drill, keep the pad moving so the plastic does not overheat.
stopIf: There is water or a crack inside the headlight.
The haze is on the inside of the lens.

sources.title: How To Clean Foggy Headlights at Home | AAA Automotive
sources.quote: One of the best ways to clean your foggy headlights is to go to an auto store and purchase a headlight restoration kit.

guides.name: Polish out a light paint scratch
steps: Drag a fingernail across the scratch; if it does not catch, you can try polishing it.
Wash and dry the area so no grit is left on it.
Test the product on a small, hidden spot first.
Put a little on a microfiber cloth and rub across the scratch with firm, even pressure.
Wipe off the residue and check; repeat a few times at most.
safety: Too many passes can wear through the clear coat.
stopIf: Your fingernail catches in the scratch, or you can see primer or bare metal.
The scratch runs across several panels.

sources.title: How To Use A Car Paint Scratch Remover | Turtle Wax | Turtle Wax Store
sources.quote: If deeper scratches catch your nail, you may need help from a professional detailer or repair shop.

guides.name: Pull a shallow dent with a suction cup
steps: Check the dent: wide, shallow, smooth dents with no crease work best.
Clean and dry the panel and the suction cup.
Press the cup onto the center of the dent and lock the handle to create suction.
Pull straight out with short, steady tugs until the dent pops; do not yank.
Release the cup and repeat around the edges if needed.
safety: Pulling too hard can crack the paint or make the dent worse.
stopIf: The dent has a sharp crease, sits on a body line or panel edge, or the paint is cracked.

guides.name: Fill a windshield chip with a repair kit
steps: Make sure the chip is under one inch, or the crack under 12 inches, in the outer glass only.
Work in the shade: clean the glass and pick loose bits out of the chip with a pin.
Center the kit's applicator over the chip and stick it down.
Add the resin and work the plunger as the kit says to push air out and resin in.
Remove the applicator, cover the spot with a curing strip and leave it in direct sun for hours.
Scrape off extra resin with the razor blade and clean the glass.
safety: Keep resin off your skin and eyes, and handle the razor blade with care.
stopIf: The chip is wider than one inch, a crack is longer than 12 inches, or the inner glass is damaged.

Pull the clog out with a finger, pencil, or wire. Screw the plug back in.
